# Results (generated by scripts/run_analysis.py)

## 1. Data checks
- Players: gate_30 = 44,700, gate_40 = 45,489
- Sample ratio check (50/50 planned): chi2 = 6.90, p = 0.0086
- Largest game-round counts: [49854, 2961, 2640]
- Players with 0 rounds: 3,994

## 2. Primary metric: day-7 retention
- gate_30: 19.02%   gate_40: 18.20%
- Difference (gate_40 - gate_30): -0.82 pp (95% CI -1.33 pp to -0.31 pp)
- Relative change: -4.3%   z = -3.16   p = 0.0016
- Bootstrap 95% CI: -1.34 pp to -0.31 pp
- Decision rule (threshold +0.50 pp): **inconclusive**. Inconclusive: the data cannot rule out a meaningful effect either way.

## 3. Secondary metrics
- Day-1 retention: 44.82% vs 44.23%, diff -0.59 pp (95% CI -1.24 pp to +0.06 pp), p = 0.0744
- Game rounds, Mann-Whitney U (robust to outliers): p = 0.0502; medians 17 vs 16
- Game rounds, Welch t-test after removing the top 0.1%: diff -0.10 rounds (95% CI -1.31 to +1.11), p = 0.8699
- Holm-adjusted p-values for the three secondary tests: rounds_mw = 0.1506, day1 = 0.1506, rounds_welch_trim = 0.8699

## 4. Power
- With 44,700 players per group and a baseline of 19.02%, the smallest effect detectable at 80% power is about +0.74 pp.
- Detecting +0.50 pp needs about 97,682 players per group.
